question: When a typed simulator supplies known dye-layer density and scanner mixing, does inversion in the correct physical order recover cross-layer correlation while scanner-RGB residual correlation remains confounded?

primary_basis.title: Emulating Emulsion: A Compact Physically-Based Model for Film Colour
primary_basis.relevance: Separates film-layer response from a later scanner matrix, motivating layer-domain inference before scanner-domain interpretation.

primary_basis.title: FGA-NN: Film Grain Analysis Neural Network
primary_basis.relevance: Latest directly relevant grain-analysis work retains explicit component-specific conventional synthesis parameters rather than an unconstrained RGB image generator.

simulation.order: correlated developed-density residual -> transmittance -> scanner matrix -> correct or wrong inverse -> optical density residual

metrics.correlation_error: off-diagonal Frobenius RMSE against the frozen layer correlation

forbidden: fit or alter either scanner matrix after observing confirmation
repair, clip or shrink correlation matrices
infer calibrated dye-layer coupling from archival scanner RGB
map the synthetic result to a stock, scanner profile, renderer default or product state
claim_ceiling: Controlled float64 simulator evidence about correlation-domain identifiability under a known invertible scanner matrix; not measured dye-layer correlation, scanner calibration, photographic quality or product evidence.
